Lore is a free and open-source personal knowledge management (PKM) application that prioritizes data sovereignty and agentic workflows. Developed by Erez Shahaf in 2026, Lore utilizes a local-first Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG 2.0) architecture to provide a private "second brain" that operates without cloud dependency or telemetry.
User Experience and Flow
Unlike traditional "vault-based" PKM tools like Obsidian or Logseq, which require users to manually create files, folders, and backlinks, Lore is designed for "One-Click Capture."
The software utilizes a HUD-style command bar that can be summoned instantly via a global hotkey. This "Flow-State" UX allows users to input information—ranging from fleeting thoughts to complex technical snippets—without context-switching or exiting their current application. Lore's background autonomous agent then performs semantic indexing, meaning the user never has to decide "where" a note lives; the software retrieves it based on conceptual relevance rather than file path.
Technical Features
Lore integrates several "Sovereign AI" technologies to ensure performance on consumer-grade hardware:
* Model Context Protocol (MCP): Lore supports the Model Context Protocol, allowing it to securely "see" and interact with other local data sources (like Git repositories or local databases) to provide grounded answers.
* Local LLM Orchestration: By leveraging Ollama, Lore supports Small Language Models (SLMs) such as Gemma and Qwen, optimized for low VRAM usage.
* Semantic Memory Layer: Utilizing LanceDB, Lore maintains a persistent vector memory that enables "Ambient Retrieval," surfacing relevant past notes as a user types in real-time.
Philosophy
The project is a leading example of Privacy-by-Design, rejecting the "Cloud AI" model where user data is treated as training material for large corporations. It positions itself as a "Permissionless" tool, meaning it requires no API keys, no subscriptions, and no internet connection to function at full capacity.
